newsitem.title: TURKEY: FOCUS-Turkish shares boosted by PM's resignation.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Turkish shares boosted by PM's resignation.

text.p: Turkish shares jumped on Thursday amid market relief at the resignation of embattled Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
But brokers said apprehension over the outcome of talks on forming a new government tempered the positive trend.

The IMKB National-100 index ended the morning session up 1.98 percent, or 31 points, at 1,596 after slipping back from a high of 1,603. Trading volume rose to 8.49 trillion lira ($58 million) from 4.46 trillion on Wednesday morning.
Wednesday evening's resignation by Erbakan fuelled hopes of an end in sight to months of political uncertainty which have dogged the share market.
The main market index declined 5.2 percent last week and continued to fall earlier this week.
"The market will sustain a steady upward trend. I believe the way is open for the index to rise to the 1,720 point level," said broker Hakan Demirbulak of Tat Securities.
However, psychological resistance at the 1,600 point level halted the uptrend on Thursday, brokers said.
Profit-taking may erode the gains during the afternoon as the wait continues for the formation of an expected caretaker government to lead the country into early polls, they said.

"The market will set out a new course in line with the political developments. Until there is a clear signal from Ankara, the market will remain restrained," said Mustafa Toprak, a broker at Es Securities.

President Suleyman Demirel began talks with opposition leaders on Thursday in a bid to replace Erbakan, pushed into resigning by a campaign against Islamist activism which the military launched in February.

Some brokers said the market's advance was a response to speculation that Demirel might give the government mandate to main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz rather than Erbakan's conservative coalition partner Tansu Ciller.
"There is a buying trend but investors are still cautious. They now discount the expectation that Demirel will not ask Ciller to form the government," said Ismet Palanli from Ar Securities.
Brokers said selective demand in state shares fuelled the gains. Trading was most active in utilities Aktas Elektrik and Cukurova Elektrik and oil refiner Tupras.

The strongest gains were posted by tourism sector shares, which rose 3.75 percent, while the index of financial stocks was up 3.18 percent. But Gokhan Kolay of Polen Securities said caution was advisable.
"Six month financial results will be announced soon. But there are still political uncertainties. My recommendation to investors is that they should not buy stocks for a while more," he said.
Elsewhere in financial markets, the lira continued its decline against the dollar, slipping to 145,900 to the U.S. currency from 145,500 on Wednesday.
A fall in bond yields to 106-106.5 percent from Wednesday's 111 percent level was more a response to decreasing funding costs rather than easing political tension, bankers said.
